issue_context.title: Could cv::Mat be nothrow movable?
issue_context.body:
### Describe the feature and motivation

A Folly user has noticed that `Mat(Mat&&)` is noexcept(false). This means that it gets the ["vector pessimization"](https://quuxplusone.github.io/blog/2022/08/26/vector-pessimization/) with `std::vector` (making copies on reallocation rather than moving), and it can't be put into a `folly::fbvector<cv::Mat>` at all (https://github.com/facebook/folly/issues/1821), because Folly actually asserts at compile time that moving can be done without throwing exceptions.

Looking at the code, I don't see any _obvious_ reason `Mat(Mat&&)` couldn't just be replaced with `Mat(Mat&&) CV_NOEXCEPT`. But there might be a _subtle_ reason? If so, it would be great to document that reason with a code comment on the declaration and/or definition of the throwing move constructor, so that people don't ask this question again. :)

### Additional context

_No response_
comments: After reviewing the code for [cv::Mat::Mat(Mat&&)](https://github.com/opencv/opencv/blob/f9c3c3d66689443bb8dcff4e3c90a35e0d63617b/modules/core/src/matrix.cpp#L598-L620), I think we can investigate whether [```cv::MatSize```](https://github.com/opencv/opencv/blob/f9c3c3d66689443bb8dcff4e3c90a35e0d63617b/modules/core/include/opencv2/core/mat.hpp#L587-L599) and [```cv::MatStep```](https://github.com/opencv/opencv/blob/f9c3c3d66689443bb8dcff4e3c90a35e0d63617b/modules/core/include/opencv2/core/mat.hpp#L601-L614) can have nothrow move constructors. In the higher dimensional matrix case (```dims() >= 3```) both structs contain pointers to some heap-allocated buffers.

@kinchungwong: Maybe I don't understand the code's organization, but, just looking at the header files you linked to ([MatSize](https://github.com/opencv/opencv/blob/f9c3c3d66689443bb8dcff4e3c90a35e0d63617b/modules/core/include/opencv2/core/mat.hpp#L587-L599), [MatStep](https://github.com/opencv/opencv/blob/f9c3c3d66689443bb8dcff4e3c90a35e0d63617b/modules/core/include/opencv2/core/mat.hpp#L601-L614)) — it looks to me like we already have `is_trivially_copyable_v<cv::MatSize>` and `is_trivially_move_constructible_v<cv::MatStep>`. (`MatStep` does have a protected non-trivial copy-assignment operator, but its move and copy constructors are both implicitly defaulted and trivial.) So those aren't the blockers — unless I'm missing something!

> So those aren't the blockers

Thanks, I should have provided the snippets for ```MatSize``` and ```MatStep``` method implementations. Here's [```MatSize::operator==(const MatSize&)```](https://github.com/opencv/opencv/blob/f9c3c3d66689443bb8dcff4e3c90a35e0d63617b/modules/core/src/matrix.cpp#L203-L216)

While I was searching for these method implementations, I do notice that there are [non-member methods directly involved in the buffer allocations of MatStep.](https://github.com/opencv/opencv/blob/f9c3c3d66689443bb8dcff4e3c90a35e0d63617b/modules/core/src/matrix.cpp#L218)

I see that it is possibly a violation of [Law of Demeter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Law_of_Demeter) that complicates my attempt to analyze the situation. I'm not in a position to criticize, but I'm also not confident enough to say whether it would have been safe to change the nothrow classification of the two structs. The LoD problem also makes it difficult to search for instances - I'd have to build the full project in order to detect all instances where non-members directly interfere with the allocations inside MatSize and MatStep. (I apologize that I don't have time for this currently.)

My understanding of nothrow is that we the programmers are ultimately responsible for the safety and correctness of the outcomes. If we classify them as nothrow, and if that leads to buggy scenarios, we cannot blame the compilers. Perhaps I need more time to study the situation.

> I'm not in a position to criticize, but I'm also not confident enough to say

Well, that makes two of us. ;) I'm definitely not familiar with the OpenCV codebase at all, so I recognize that you've taken on the harder job here of pointing at stuff, whereas I've got the easier job of just looking at each thing you indicate and saying "Nope... nope..."

For example: [`MatSize::operator==`](https://github.com/opencv/opencv/blob/f9c3c3d66689443bb8dcff4e3c90a35e0d63617b/modules/core/src/matrix.cpp#L203-L216) definitely never throws, _and_ definitely is never called from [`Mat`'s move-constructor](https://github.com/opencv/opencv/blob/f9c3c3d66689443bb8dcff4e3c90a35e0d63617b/modules/core/src/matrix.cpp#L598-L620), so it's not the problem, for both those reasons at once.

[`setSize(Mat&, ~~~)`](https://github.com/opencv/opencv/blob/f9c3c3d66689443bb8dcff4e3c90a35e0d63617b/modules/core/src/matrix.cpp#L218) definitely _does_ throw (because it calls `fastMalloc`), but it's never called from [`Mat`'s move-constructor](https://github.com/opencv/opencv/blob/f9c3c3d66689443bb8dcff4e3c90a35e0d63617b/modules/core/src/matrix.cpp#L598-L620), so it's not the problem.

Absolutely the _only_ way that [`Mat(Mat&&)`](https://github.com/opencv/opencv/blob/f9c3c3d66689443bb8dcff4e3c90a35e0d63617b/modules/core/src/matrix.cpp#L598-L620) could _ever_ throw an exception, is if it were to call a function that throws. And AFAICT it doesn't call any functions. So it can't throw. (Am I missing anything?) The existence of _other_ functions in the codebase that use exceptions is irrelevant to whether `Mat(Mat&&)` _itself_ could possibly throw.

> My understanding of nothrow is that we the programmers are ultimately responsible for the safety and correctness of the outcomes. If we classify them as nothrow, and if that leads to buggy scenarios, we cannot blame the compilers.

You're correct about that. If it _were_ possible for `Mat(Mat&&)` to throw, it'd be a pretty bad bug to mark it `noexcept`. (Or, if it doesn't throw _today_ but you want to leave the door open for it to throw _tomorrow_, then it'd be undesirable to commit to `noexcept` today. But my prior probability on that is very low: a move-constructor that throws when it doesn't have to is always a bad idea, for exactly the reason above (`std::vector` pessimization + incompatibility with many third-party libraries).)
@Quuxplusone I agree with all points in your analysis.
Indeed, trivial members are just copied over, it can totally be marked as noexcept

review_comments:
What about assertion in the else branch?
```
CV_Assert(m.step.p != m.step.buf);
```
I forgot CV_Assert was more than an assert ... If it can throw, I guess it won't work indeed.

I see, `CV_Assert` calls `cv::error` calls `throw` ([here](https://github.com/opencv/opencv/blob/4.x/modules/core/src/system.cpp#L1276)).
But still, IIUC, isn't that `CV_Assert` basically asserting an _invariant?_ I mean, IIUC, you're not actually trying to use that exception for control-flow. IIUC, you expect that `(m.step.p != m.step.buf)` will be true literally every time that line is hit. So it would be perfectly appropriate to replace that line with whatever macro OpenCV uses to express invariants. (In most codebases the invariant-checking macro _is_ spelled `assert`, which is why that `CV_Assert` looked harmless at first glance.)

If OpenCV _has_ no invariant-checking macro a la `assert`, then I suggest it would be perfectly appropriate to simply eliminate that line, or replace it with a comment.

Actually, why even modify `m`? `m` is moved so there is not point in modifying it. `Move constructors typically "steal" the resources held by the argument (e.g. pointers to dynamically-allocated objects, file descriptors, TCP sockets, I/O streams, running threads, etc.) rather than make copies of them, and leave the argument in some valid but otherwise indeterminate state.` https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/language/move_constructor

> why even modify `m`

It is modified to transfer ownership of allocated metadata buffers. To avoid use-after-free when `m` destructor is called.

> CV_Assert

Basically it checks `invariant` and should never fail.
I believe we could replace failure handling code with `abort()` / `std::terminate()`.
